title: Separating overlapping sources and listening to held-out real recordings
reader: Signed-in local Codex CLI, isolated ephemeral gpt-6.1-terra low-reasoning sessions, no shell, network tools, filenames, source labels, pictures of the scene or human reference answers. This image client received local audio reports and spectra, without waveform attachments.

protocol.mixtures: 48 held-out 4 s mixtures of 96 different FSD50K evaluation source files outside the example bank. Development used 16 other pairs. Hash-order the eligible prior source-identity recordings by SHA-256 of reel-overlapping-sources-v1/ plus source ID. Pair recordings from distinct uploaders with different human source labels. First channel resampled to 16 kHz, highest-energy 4 s crop at 0.5 s hops, RMS 0.06 for the louder source. Relative levels cycle through 0, -3, -6, -9 dB. A common scale caps the peak at 0.9. No clean references or candidate names reach the separator. Match the strongest MixIT estimate and mix minus that estimate one-to-one to the two clean waveforms, maximizing total SI-SDR. SI-SDR improvements concern signal quality; the assignment uses the references only in evaluation.
protocol.naming: First 24 mixtures by ID, and the original isolated tracks of the first six pairs as 12 controls, chosen before hearing responses. Frozen prior = verified source examples and original spectrum. Whole adds open Audio Flamingo impression. Split adds original, top layer and remainder reports and spectra from the production listen_layer tool with no source proposal or rank. The two latter arms retain the same example evidence. All use the same reader and up-to-two-names question. Unmatched claims need not be absent from the original source files. Single controls isolate recordings, each of which may contain multiple events.
protocol.field: 51 real first-channel four-second intervals from ten TUT Sound Events 2016 evaluation field recordings, same intervals as focused-listening.json. Target labels are the short, fully contained human-annotated events used in that trial. Whole and split use identical unmodified room sound. No example-reader hints for either arm. Unmatched sounds can be present elsewhere in the annotations or recording.
protocol.grading: An independent ephemeral gpt-6.1-terra (medium) graded unique reference-label/answer pairs in SHA-256 order without the audio, version or file identifiers. E means same identifiable source or action, P compatible without strict identification, O other. The primary count allows one strict match per claim and per reference. Entire-file human labels can be less specific than a real sound. Full grading matrices below permit alternate scoring.
protocol.name_question: Which distinct sources or sound actions are audible in this recording? Give up to two specific names supported by the audio. Only include a second when you can distinguish it from the first. If you cannot identify any, return an empty list.
protocol.caption_metric: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 at 1110a243fdf4706b3f48f1d95db1a4f5529b4d41. For each recording subtract mean semantic similarity to other recordings’ captions from mean similarity to the five captions for that recording. Divide the across-recording mean by the matching-minus-other gap when a held-out human caption is the reader. Panels have their own distractors. Bootstrap whole recordings, 10000 draws. Cosines and top-1 scores by recording below; official human captions are available from Clotho. Overall human perception is not measured.
protocol.panel_known: Previous 24-recording panel reused for continuity. Prior = earlier lightweight stream, new = same stream plus one open native replay. Extra replay and reader both change. This is not a comparison of the full Qwen model against Audio Flamingo.
protocol.panel_fresh: 16 new Clotho evaluation/Clotho-AQA test recordings outside earlier benchmarks and the reference bank, distinct uploaders outside the old panel. Four official questions and three votes each. One complete open replay and the same spectrum per case. Prior is the frozen CoNeTTE fallback with the Qwen environment unavailable. Waveform is Audio Flamingo Next. Both is the same waveform report plus the exact independent CoNeTTE scene from the other arm, equivalent to independent_caption=true. Both was explored after seeing differences between the single readers.
protocol.panel_replication: 16 further recordings held out from both panels and their uploaders. Hash seed reel-waveform-readers-replication-v1/. Four official questions sampled by SHA-256(file/question), each with three human yes/no votes. Prior and both run through their actual released-range listen entry points. Same spectrum, GPT prompt and individual session conditions. Unknown receives zero. The question-conditioned and negative controls use the same questions and votes.
protocol.setup: Research model audio-cpp/Audio-Flamingo-GGUF Q4_K, NVIDIA Audio Flamingo Next, Apple M4 Pro 64 GiB. The same-machine full Qwen3-Omni 30B 8-bit comparison stopped under memory pressure before producing a score.
protocol.specific_questions: In the independent replication panel, the question-conditioned listen received the four official questions as a single short request. Its before_question and scene fields are independent of the questions. Actual production MCP captured all three and the original spectrum. Another isolated GPT chose yes, no or unknown. Conditions: same questions on the correct audio, same questions on a different recording rotated by seven in the panel, and no audio or listening report. Cluster bootstrap the differences by recording, 20000 draws. Prior and open are the preceding unprompted replays. A correct answer after swapping the recording can arise by coincidence or a question prior. No calibration on these answers.
protocol.door: Audio-only real MCP view_media and listen on A, B, C and a digital-silence control. All stopped at 8.5 s. A and C differ after the cutoff. The SHA-256 covers the full listening report and spectrum hash. C reused A’s GPT response after exact input equality. All four requests for the interval 8.4–8.6 s were rejected.
